narrative.title: Tallying Every Load Combination on the Loading Ramp
narrative.scenario: A freight planner wants to see the weight of every possible load that could leave the ramp, where a load is any subset of the parked pallets — including the empty truck. Walking the pallet line once and branching take-or-skip at each pallet produces the full ledger of load weights, which the planner then reads in ascending order.
narrative.inputFormat: An array arr of N non-negative integers.
narrative.outputFormat: The sum of every subset, sorted in ascending order.

complexity.optimalTime: O(2^N) branch walks plus O(2^N log 2^N) for the sort
complexity.optimalSpace: O(N) recursion depth beyond the output

testCases.explanation: Take nothing (0), either pallet alone (2, 3), or both (5), then read in order.
Eight subsets, and their sums happen to run cleanly from 0 to 8.

hintLevels: Level 1: You never need the subsets themselves — only their sums, so carry a single number down the recursion.
Level 2: At each index either add the element to the running sum or leave it; both branches advance the index.
Level 3: The two-branch recursion naturally produces 2^N leaves; sorting afterwards is the only step the DFS does not give you for free.
